name: Massachusetts

statute.name: Massachusetts Public Records Law
statute.citation: G.L. c. 66, § 10; definition at G.L. c. 4, § 7, cl. 26; regs 950 CMR 32.00

response.rule_text: Custodian must respond within 10 business days of receiving the request, G.L. c. 66, § 10(a); a custodian may ask the Supervisor of Records for more time (within 20 business days of the request) but must still send an initial response in 10 business days.

fees.labor_rule: No charge for the first four hours (state agencies; municipalities over 20,000 first two hours); not more than $25/hour thereafter; no fee for segregation/redaction unless required by law (950 CMR 32.07).
fees.copy_rule: Reasonable actual copying cost (schedule not extracted).
fees.waiver_rule: Custodian may consider fee waiver requests (public interest); fees are waived if the custodian fails to respond to the initial request in 10 business days.
fees.late_penalty: Fees are waived if custodian does not respond within 10 business days.

residency.rule_text: 'Any person' may request, G.L. c. 66, § 10(a); appears to include non-residents; custodian may not ask about status or motive (950 CMR 32.06(1)(h)).

appeal.body: Supervisor of Public Records (Secretary of the Commonwealth); or Superior Court
appeal.rule_text: Optional administrative appeal to the Supervisor of Records within 90 calendar days of the response, G.L. c. 66, § 10(b); 950 CMR 32.08. The Supervisor can order compliance but has no enforcement power (may refer to AG/DA); requester may instead go to court.

notes: Appeal type classification is my judgement (Supervisor can order but not enforce). Governor held not explicitly covered by the law (SJC) and the Supervisor says governor's records are not subject; legislature and courts not subject. Universities/school districts not confirmed as rule. Extension amounts beyond request-to-Supervisor not extracted.
